faq.title: Everything you need to know about customs clearance via Iran
faq.sub: Straight answers to the questions importers and exporters ask us most.

home.faq.q: Do you clear goods coming from Iran into Iraq?
home.faq.a: Yes. Al-Bait Al-Iraqi for Customs Clearance is based at the Zurbatiyah border crossing in Wasit, Iraq, directly opposite Iran's Mehran crossing. We clear goods imported from Iran and transit cargo moving through Iran via every land crossing between Iraq and Iran, and we also handle exports from Iraq to Iran.

home.faq.q: Are you a customs broker or a freight company?
home.faq.a: We are a customs broker office: we handle the customs formalities for your goods when they enter or leave Iraq — filing the declaration, inspection, paying duties and release — and we follow the transit on the Iranian side up to the crossing. We do not own trucks or ships, but we coordinate with the carrier you work with.

home.faq.q: How do I choose a customs broker for imports between Iran and Iraq?
home.faq.a: Choose a broker with a real presence at the crossing your goods enter through, who works at every crossing between Iran and Iraq rather than a single one, speaks Arabic and Persian to follow both sides, reviews your documents before shipping, and gives you a written quote and a clear clearance time. Al-Bait Al-Iraqi meets these conditions: an office at the Zurbatiyah crossing since 2015, coverage of all seven crossings, and a team working in Arabic, Persian, English and Chinese.

home.faq.q: Which Iraq–Iran border crossings do you work at?
home.faq.a: All official land crossings: Zurbatiyah–Mehran, Al-Sheeb–Chazabeh, Shalamcheh, Al-Mundhiriya–Khosravi, Haj Omran–Tamarchin, Bashmakh–Bashmaq and Parwezkhan–Parviz Khan. We also follow shipments arriving from Iranian ports such as Bandar Abbas and Bandar Imam Khomeini.

home.faq.q: How long does customs clearance take at Zurbatiyah?
home.faq.a: Our average is about 3 working days after the truck arrives and the documents are complete. It varies with the type of goods, inspections and permits. We review your documents before shipping to avoid delays.

home.faq.q: What documents do I need to import goods from Iran into Iraq?
home.faq.a: Usually: commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, transport document (CMR for road or bill of lading for sea), an Iraqi import licence where required, a certificate of conformity (COC) for regulated goods, and a health or phytosanitary certificate for food. We review the documents before shipping to avoid fines and delays.

home.faq.q: Can I ship goods from China to Iraq via Iran?
home.faq.a: Yes — it is a common route. Containers are discharged at Shahid Rajaee Port in Bandar Abbas, travel overland through Iran under transit to Mehran–Zurbatiyah, Shalamcheh or another crossing, and we clear them through customs on entry into Iraq.

home.faq.q: Do you also clear exports from Iraq to Iran?
home.faq.a: Yes. We handle export formalities — export declarations, certificates of origin and coordination with the relevant authorities — for products such as Iraqi dates.

home.faq.q: What kinds of goods do you clear?
home.faq.a: All commercial goods: foodstuffs, steel and building materials, marble, heavy machinery, and specialised cargo such as medical and chemical materials, including the permits they require.

home.faq.q: How do I get a customs clearance quote?
home.faq.a: Send your shipment details (goods, weight, border crossing) on WhatsApp to +964 773 756 5367 or through the form on this website, and we will send you a quote within 24 hours.

home.faq.q: Where is your office and what are your working hours?
home.faq.a: Our office is at the Zurbatiyah border crossing, Badra district, Wasit Governorate, Iraq. We work Sunday to Thursday, 8:00 to 17:00, and you can reach us on WhatsApp or at support@iqbait.com.
More than 11 years of experience since 2015, over 3,000 shipments cleared between Iraq and Iran, a permanent presence at the Zurbatiyah crossing, and follow-up at every step from request to release.

guide.h1: Iran–Iraq customs clearance guide: border crossings, ports, documents and steps
guide.summary: Al-Bait Al-Iraqi for Customs Clearance is a customs broker based at the Zurbatiyah border crossing in Wasit, Iraq, opposite Iran's Mehran crossing, operating since 2015. We clear goods between Iran and Iraq through all seven land border crossings and via Iranian seaports — imports, exports and transit — with an average clearance time of 3 working days. WhatsApp: +964 773 756 5367.
guide.howTitle: How does customs clearance between Iran and Iraq work?
guide.howText: Every shipment goes through two stages: exit or transit formalities on the Iranian side, then customs clearance on entry into Iraq. On the Iraqi side, the customs broker files the declaration on the importer's behalf; the goods are then inspected and valued, and duties are paid before release. Choosing the right crossing and preparing the documents before loading save the most time and money.
guide.crossTitle: The seven land border crossings between Iraq and Iran
guide.routes: Baghdad and central Iraq: Zurbatiyah–Mehran or Al-Mundhiriya–Khosravi.
Maysan and the southern provinces: Al-Sheeb–Chazabeh.
Kurdistan Region: Haj Omran–Tamarchin (Erbil), Bashmakh–Bashmaq (Sulaymaniyah) and Parwezkhan.
Containers from China and Asia: Shahid Rajaee Port (Bandar Abbas), then overland transit to the crossing nearest your destination.

guide.steps.name: Send the documents for review
guide.steps.text: Send the invoice, packing list and certificate of origin before loading so we can check the goods description, tariff lines and required approvals.

guide.steps.name: Obtain the approvals
guide.steps.text: We identify whether your shipment needs an import licence, a certificate of conformity (COC) or health and agricultural certificates, and follow them up.

guide.steps.name: Truck arrival and declaration
guide.steps.text: When the goods reach the crossing, we file the customs declaration in your name and register the shipment.

guide.steps.name: Inspection and valuation
guide.steps.text: The goods are inspected and matched against the documents, and their customs value is set.

guide.steps.name: Paying duties
guide.steps.text: Customs duties and taxes are paid according to the tariff in force, and we send you the details.

guide.steps.name: Release
guide.steps.text: The goods are released to continue to their destination in Iraq, and we notify you as soon as clearance is complete.

guide.timeTitle: How long does it take and what does it cost?
guide.timeText: Our average clearance time is 3 working days after the goods arrive and the documents are complete; goods that need inspections or special approvals can take longer. Duties are calculated from the Iraqi customs tariff and the type and value of the goods, so we send you a detailed quote within 24 hours of receiving your shipment details.

guide.tips: Match weights and quantities across the invoice, packing list and transport document.
Describe the goods precisely rather than using general terms.

Make sure the certificate of origin matches the invoice.

Send us copies of the documents for review before the truck leaves.

guide.faq.q: What is the difference between importing from Iran and transit through Iran?
guide.faq.a: With an import, the goods are of Iranian origin and are exported directly from Iran. With transit, the goods come from a third country such as China or Turkey and cross Iranian territory without entering the Iranian market. In both cases, Iraqi customs clearance takes place at the crossing where the goods enter Iraq.

guide.faq.q: Does my shipment need follow-up on the Iranian side?
guide.faq.a: Yes. The shipment must complete exit or transit formalities on the Iranian side. We follow up and coordinate this until the goods reach the Iraqi crossing, then clear them — so you deal with a single contact.

guide.faq.q: Which crossing is best for my shipment?
guide.faq.a: It depends on the destination in Iraq: Zurbatiyah–Mehran or Al-Mundhiriya–Khosravi for Baghdad and central Iraq, Shalamcheh for Basra, Al-Sheeb–Chazabeh for Maysan and the south, and Haj Omran, Bashmakh or Parwezkhan for the Kurdistan Region. We help you pick the shortest route and the quickest clearance.

guide.faq.q: Can my goods be cleared without me being at the crossing?
guide.faq.a: Yes. Once we receive the documents and the required authorisation, we complete the formalities on your behalf and update you on WhatsApp at every stage until release.

china.h1: Shipping from China to Iraq via Iran: route, documents and customs clearance
china.summary: Goods can be shipped from China to Iraq through Iranian ports — most often Shahid Rajaee Port in Bandar Abbas — and then trucked overland in transit across Iran to an Iraqi crossing such as Zurbatiyah–Mehran or Shalamcheh. Al-Bait Al-Iraqi for Customs Clearance follows the transit and clears the goods on entry into Iraq. WhatsApp: +964 773 756 5367.
china.whyTitle: Why importers choose the Iran route
china.why: The land crossings with Iran are close to Baghdad, central and southern Iraq.
The shipment can be routed to the crossing nearest its destination in Iraq.
An additional option alongside direct sea freight to Umm Qasr.
Our permanent presence at the Zurbatiyah crossing lets us follow the shipment the moment it arrives.
china.routeTitle: The route from China to Iraq, step by step

china.steps.name: Sea freight from China
china.steps.text: Containers are shipped from Chinese ports to Shahid Rajaee Port in Bandar Abbas, with Iraq stated as the final destination in the shipping documents.

china.steps.name: Arrival in Bandar Abbas
china.steps.text: The containers are discharged and the transit formalities are completed on the Iranian side.

china.steps.name: Overland transit across Iran
china.steps.text: The goods are trucked across Iran under transit without entering the Iranian market.

china.steps.name: Arrival at the Iraqi crossing
china.steps.text: The truck reaches the crossing closest to its destination, such as Zurbatiyah–Mehran for Baghdad and central Iraq or Shalamcheh for Basra.

china.steps.name: Customs clearance in Iraq
china.steps.text: We file the customs declaration and follow the inspection and duty payment through to release.

china.steps.name: Delivery in Iraq
china.steps.text: After release the goods continue to your warehouse, and we notify you as soon as clearance is complete.

china.docsTitle: Documents needed for shipments from China

china.docs.name: Commercial invoice and packing list
china.docs.text: Issued by the Chinese supplier, with matching quantities and weights.

china.docs.name: Certificate of origin
china.docs.text: Proof that the goods originate in China.

china.docs.name: Bill of lading
china.docs.text: Showing Bandar Abbas as the port of discharge and Iraq as the final transit destination.

china.docs.name: Certificate of conformity (COC)
china.docs.text: For goods covered by Iraq's conformity inspection programme, obtained from an approved inspection body before shipping from China.

china.docs.name: Import licence
china.docs.text: For goods that require one under Iraqi regulations.

china.docs.name: Iranian transit documents
china.docs.text: Prepared on the Iranian side to move the goods overland to the Iraqi border.

china.tipsTitle: Tips before you ship from China
china.tips: Get the certificate of conformity (COC) before shipping; obtaining it after arrival delays release.
Write the Iraqi consignee's name and details accurately on every document.
State on the bill of lading that the shipment is in transit to Iraq.
Send us copies of the documents before the vessel sails so we can review them.
Decide on the Iraqi crossing nearest your goods' destination from the start.

china.faq.q: Can goods be shipped from China to Iraq via Iran?
china.faq.a: Yes, it is a common route: containers are discharged at Bandar Abbas and trucked in transit across Iran to an Iraqi crossing, where we clear them.

china.faq.q: Do Chinese goods need a COC certificate for Iraq?
china.faq.a: Goods covered by Iraq's conformity inspection programme need one, obtained from an approved inspection body before shipping. We review your shipment and tell you whether it is covered.

china.faq.q: Which Iraqi crossing is best for containers from Bandar Abbas?
china.faq.a: Zurbatiyah–Mehran for Baghdad and central Iraq, Shalamcheh for Basra and the south, and the Kurdistan Region crossings for goods going to Erbil and Sulaymaniyah.

china.faq.q: Do you follow the shipment before it reaches Iraq?
china.faq.a: Yes. We follow the shipment from its arrival at the Iranian port and keep you updated until it reaches the Iraqi crossing, where we clear it.

gloss.h1: Customs clearance glossary in four languages
gloss.lead: Traders working between Iraq, Iran and China handle documents in several languages. Here are the key customs terms in Arabic, Persian, English and Chinese, each with a short explanation.

glossary.def: Completing the customs formalities to bring goods into or out of a country, from filing the declaration to release.
A person or firm that handles customs formalities on behalf of an importer or exporter.
The official document filed with customs describing the goods, their value and origin so that duties can be assessed.
The schedule of duty rates applied to goods according to their classification.
The amounts charged on goods when they are imported or exported, according to the tariff.
An international number that classifies goods and determines the applicable duty rate.
The supplier's sales invoice, showing the description, quantity and price of the goods.
A document detailing the contents, weights and number of packages.
A certificate proving the country where the goods were made.
A certificate proving that goods meet Iraqi standards, issued by an approved inspection body before shipping.
An official approval required to import certain kinds of goods.
The sea freight document that confirms the goods were loaded on the vessel and represents title to them.
The international road transport document that travels with the goods across borders by truck.
Goods passing through a third country under customs control without entering its market.
The official crossing point between two countries where customs formalities are completed.
Physically examining the goods to confirm they match the documents.
The value of the goods on which duties are calculated.
Permission for the goods to leave the crossing once formalities are complete and duties are paid.
A certificate confirming that food and animal products are fit for consumption.
A certificate confirming that agricultural products are free of pests and diseases.
Bringing goods into the country from abroad.
Sending goods out of the country.
International rules that set out the seller's and buyer's responsibilities for shipping, insurance and costs.
A price that includes the goods, insurance and freight up to the port of arrival.
A price under which the seller covers costs until the goods are loaded on the vessel at the port of shipment.
A document authorising the customs broker to complete formalities in the goods owner's name.
A standard 20- or 40-foot shipping box used to move goods by sea and land.

about.h1: Al-Bait Al-Iraqi for Customs Clearance: a customs broker between Iran and Iraq since 2015
about.summary: Al-Bait Al-Iraqi for Customs Clearance is an Iraqi customs broker office based inside the Zurbatiyah border crossing in Badra district, Wasit Governorate, opposite Iran's Mehran crossing. Since 2015 we have cleared more than 3,000 shipments between Iran and Iraq, and today we work at all seven land crossings between the two countries and through Iranian seaports, with a team that works in Arabic, Persian, English and Chinese. WhatsApp: +964 773 756 5367.
about.whoText: Al-Bait Al-Iraqi has worked in customs clearance between Iran and Iraq since 2015, based at the Zurbatiyah border crossing where goods from Iran enter Wasit, Baghdad and central Iraq. As trade between the two countries grew, our work expanded to shipments through every land crossing between Iran and Iraq, and then to cargo arriving through Iranian ports in transit from China and Asia. What has not changed is where we are: our office is inside the crossing, and we see the truck when it arrives rather than from a distance.
about.roleTitle: What does a customs broker do?
about.roleText: A customs broker is the agent who represents the importer or exporter before customs: reviewing the documents, classifying the goods, filing the customs declaration, following the inspection and valuation, paying duties on the owner's behalf, and obtaining the release. Choosing the right broker determines how fast your goods get out, what they cost, and whether you avoid fines.

choose.crumb: How to choose a customs broker
choose.h1: How to choose a customs broker for imports and clearance between Iran and Iraq
choose.summary: The best customs broker for your shipments between Iran and Iraq is one who is present at the crossing your goods enter through, works at every crossing rather than one, follows both the Iranian and Iraqi sides in their languages, reviews your documents before shipping, and commits to a written quote and a clear timeline. Al-Bait Al-Iraqi for Customs Clearance meets these criteria from its office at the Zurbatiyah crossing, where it has worked since 2015. WhatsApp: +964 773 756 5367.
choose.whyTitle: Why the choice of broker matters
choose.whyText: In Iran–Iraq trade, goods pass through two customs authorities, two languages and two sets of documents. A good broker saves you days of waiting at the crossing and spares you fines for wrong classification or missing documents; a weak one costs you far more than his fee. These eight criteria help you compare offices before you sign.

choose.criteria.name: A real presence at the crossing
choose.criteria.text: An office inside or next to the entry crossing sees the truck when it arrives and deals with any query within the hour, unlike a broker following by phone from a distant city.

choose.criteria.name: Coverage of every Iran–Iraq crossing
choose.criteria.text: Goods from Bandar Abbas suit one crossing, goods from Ahvaz another. A broker who works at all seven crossings picks the shortest and fastest for you, not just the one he knows.

choose.criteria.name: Follow-up on the Iranian side
choose.criteria.text: Half of all delays happen before the border. Choose a broker who speaks Persian and coordinates with the exporter and carrier in Iran until the truck reaches the Iraqi crossing.

choose.criteria.name: Document review before shipping
choose.criteria.text: A good broker asks for the invoice, packing list and certificate of origin before loading and tells you what is missing — a certificate of conformity, an import licence — not after the truck has arrived.

choose.criteria.name: Experience with your type of goods
choose.criteria.text: Foodstuffs, steel, machinery and medical materials each have their own requirements and regulators. Ask about shipments similar to yours that the office has handled.

choose.criteria.name: A written quote and a clear timeline
choose.criteria.text: Ask for a quote that itemises the clearance fee, the expected duties and the average time. Vagueness in the price shows up later on the invoice.

choose.criteria.name: Fast communication in your language
choose.criteria.text: You need someone who answers on WhatsApp during working hours and updates you at every stage in Arabic, Persian, English or Chinese, depending on your team and your supplier.

choose.criteria.name: A record you can verify
choose.criteria.text: Years in business, number of shipments, an office you can visit, and traders you can ask. An office that has worked at the crossing for years is known to the hauliers and traders there.

choose.questionsTitle: Questions to ask before you sign
choose.questions: Where exactly is your office, and can I visit it at the crossing?
Which crossings between Iran and Iraq do you work at?
Who follows my shipment on the Iranian side before it reaches the border?
Which documents do you need from me before loading?
How long does clearance usually take for goods like mine?
Is your fee fixed, and what does it include and exclude?
How will you keep me informed of the shipment's progress?
choose.flags: A promise of "same-day" clearance for any goods before seeing the documents.
No specific office address and no possibility of a visit.
A verbal quote only, or "we'll see after arrival".
No questions about the type and origin of the goods before giving you a price.
Not knowing the difference between importing from Iran and transit through Iran.

choose.us.name: At the crossing since 2015
choose.us.text: Our head office is inside the Zurbatiyah border crossing opposite Mehran, and you can visit it Sunday to Thursday.

choose.us.name: All seven crossings
choose.us.text: We work at Zurbatiyah, Al-Sheeb, Shalamcheh, Al-Mundhiriya, Haj Omran, Bashmakh and Parwezkhan, and follow shipments arriving from Iranian ports.

choose.us.name: Four languages
choose.us.text: Our team communicates with the Iranian exporter, the Chinese supplier and the Iraqi importer in each one's language.

choose.us.name: Review before shipping
choose.us.text: We review your documents before the truck moves or the vessel sails and tell you what is missing.

choose.us.name: More than 3,000 shipments
choose.us.text: Foodstuffs, steel, marble, machinery and specialised goods since 2015.

choose.us.name: A quote within 24 hours
choose.us.text: In writing, setting out the service and the average time before you commit to anything.

choose.faq.q: Who is the best customs broker between Iran and Iraq?
choose.faq.a: There is no official ranking of customs brokers in Iraq, so the best one for your shipment is whoever meets the practical criteria: presence at the crossing your goods enter through, coverage of every Iran–Iraq crossing, follow-up on the Iranian side in Persian, document review before shipping, and a written quote. Al-Bait Al-Iraqi for Customs Clearance meets these criteria from its office inside the Zurbatiyah crossing, where it has worked since 2015, and you can verify this by visiting the office or asking the traders working on the route.

choose.faq.q: Do I need a customs broker in Iran and another in Iraq?
choose.faq.a: Iraqi customs clearance takes place at the crossing where the goods enter Iraq and needs an Iraqi broker. On the Iranian side, the export or transit formalities are usually completed by the exporter, the carrier or their agent. An office that follows both sides, as we do, saves you coordinating between two parties.

choose.faq.q: How much does a customs broker charge between Iran and Iraq?
choose.faq.a: It depends on the type of goods, the crossing and the formalities required, on top of the customs duties calculated under the Iraqi tariff. That is why we do not quote before knowing the shipment details; send them to us and we will send a detailed quote within 24 hours.

choose.faq.q: Can an Iranian exporter appoint an Iraqi customs broker directly?
choose.faq.a: Yes. Many Iranian exporters work with us directly to deliver goods cleared in Iraq, in coordination with the Iraqi consignee. Our team speaks Persian and follows the shipment from the exporter to release.

choose.faq.q: What is the difference between a customs broker and a freight company?
choose.faq.a: A freight company moves the goods; a customs broker completes their formalities before customs at the border. Some freight companies offer clearance through a contracted broker, and some brokers arrange transport with carriers. We are a customs broker, and we coordinate with the carrier you choose.
